pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered as movement-pattern assessment from day one plus tailored five-to-fifteen-minute mobility work, tied directly to his stated goals: 'for you, that means the pull-ups get there significantly, and the handstands are also going to be definitely improving.' Response was a flat acceptance — 'Yeah, it does work' — with no questions and no elaboration, which is notable given that mobility is the subject he knows most about and has spent four years on.

The prospect pre-empted the pillar's own objections before the rep reached them — 'Macros, tracking, weighing. I've done that for eight months. After this, I was like, no' and 'I do like my pizza on the weekend sometimes' — then volunteered his full current regime and concluded 'Nutrition, I mean, we're on the same page.' Accepted rather than enthusiastic: he was confirming an existing practice, not being sold something new.

'So far, it's like the way I work. So I don't mind. I've done using the app before and recording videos when I was working with these guys, weekly checking. I've done that for multiple times with my coaches. Not only in sports, but also in business ... I have no problem with the accountability.' The pillar was pitched against the influencer-hands-off problem ('it turns out that, yeah, it's someone else'), which landed, but the prospect's acceptance is again confirmation of an existing habit, so the pillar added no new value he had to buy.

anchors.raw: I will probably take the annual subscription to do one, continue a small progression towards maybe handstands or splits or something like this
anchors.note: He is three months into a paid programme he intends to keep on an annual subscription. The incumbent is not just a price anchor, it is a time anchor — it occupies the ninety-minute gym block that is the only training window his schedule allows, so the offer is competing for the slot as much as for the money.

anchors.raw: So I did that for about six months with their online app, and then I switched to their coaching program for six months. That works immensely well because he was basically one of the guys that I used to listen to on the videos
anchors.note: He has already bought a full year of programming plus coaching from one provider and rates it as the thing that rebuilt his knee. He is a proven coaching buyer, and the sequence he bought — programme first, then coaching — is exactly the sequence he asked for here and was not offered.

anchors.raw: he started trying to add me to eat more and more supplements and stuff. He was basically trying to get me into a bodybuilder, which I didn't want to. And I told him that that's not what I wanted, and he didn't adapt the method
anchors.note: Not a number but the dominant anchor in his head: money and time already lost to a coach who would not adapt. It is the reason he will not pay upfront, and it is the anchor the OE 'burned before' move exists to dissolve.

unmet_demand.want: A self-serve programme he can buy and run before committing to coaching — his stated purchasing rule, used successfully several times, and something his setter had already told him existed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep offered only 1:1 coaching at $6,000 for six months and a $1,200 30-day version of the same coaching. Primal University, the $200/month programme product this same rep offered to a different prospect the previous day, was never mentioned, so the prospect left believing the company has no programme-only path.

unmet_demand.want: Upper-body strength work he can run alongside, not instead of, the lower-body mobility programme he is two-thirds through
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted that kettlebells train the whole body as a unit and therefore the wait 'doesn't add up', which answers a different question — the prospect's constraint is a single ninety-minute daily slot already committed, not programme overlap. Whether the coaching can be run as a genuine supplement for three months was never established either way.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that the method will work for his specific body before paying — 'I haven't tasted the method in any way, close or far'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing was offered as evidence: no client examples with comparable scoliosis or shoulder restriction, no assessment call before purchase, no testimonials. The only answer to a proof request was a paid trial.
